headlines.title: Why AEP's Plant Fight Could Make ETFs Worth A Look
headlines.summary: Owning American Electric Power Company outright means your returns hinge on its specific financial pressures. Simply Wall St flags that its interest payments are not well covered by earnings, and that a 3.04% dividend is not well covered by free cash flows. A fund that holds American Electric Power Company alongside many other businesses dilutes how much those issues or any upside in the shares can move your portfolio.

headlines.title: Utility Spending Plans Grow as Large New Power Customers Sign On
headlines.summary: American News Group News Commentary - Third-quarter results season brought larger multi-year spending plans and longer growth outlooks from several U.S. utilities as they plan for new large customers. Across their reports, companies described gigawatts of new load commitments signed, data center demand under contract, and tens of billions of dollars in planned investment in transmission, generation and distribution.

description: American Electric Power Company, Inc., an electric public utility holding company, engages in the generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity for sale to retail and wholesale customers in the United States. It operates through Vertically Integrated Utilities, Transmission and Distribution Utilities, AEP Transmission Holdco, and Generation & Marketing segments. The company generates electricity using coal and lignite, nuclear, natural gas, renewable, hydro, solar, wind, and other energy sources; owns, operates, maintains, and invests in transmission infrastructure; and engages in the retail supply, and wholesale energy trading and marketing businesses. It operates approximately 252,000 circuit miles of distribution lines; 38,000 circuit miles of transmission lines; and 25,000 MWs of regulated owned generating capacity. American Electric Power Company, Inc. was incorporated in 1906 and is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio.
